# Grothendieck Archives

> A working edition of the Alexandre Grothendieck fonds held by the University of Montpellier: the inventory of its 178 folders, read in Grothendieck's own filing order, with tools to study the working notes (dates, letters, diagrams, formulas, the hand, an index) and the findings drawn from reading them end to end. Facsimiles are not stored here: they are streamed from Montpellier at read time.

Transcriptions are machine-made and unchecked by a reader unless a file says otherwise; what this site does not claim is set out on the Method page. Statements drawn from the notes are proved in Lean 4 against Mathlib in a separate appendix.

## The fonds

- [Whole fonds](https://grothendieck.commutator.io/): the 178 folders and the reader, beside Montpellier's facsimile.
- [Index](https://grothendieck.commutator.io/index/): people, works cited and subjects, each to the folder and the batch where it occurs.
- [Timeline](https://grothendieck.commutator.io/timeline/): when the folders were written, and on what evidence.
- [Letters](https://grothendieck.commutator.io/letters/): the letters found in the folders.
- [The hand](https://grothendieck.commutator.io/hand/): words unread and doubtful, strike-outs, margins, folder by folder.
- [Diagrams](https://grothendieck.commutator.io/diagrams/) and [Formulas](https://grothendieck.commutator.io/formulas/): the commutative diagrams and displayed formulas of the notes.
- [Maps](https://grothendieck.commutator.io/maps/): folders and print, mathematical lineage, people named together, subjects, citations.
- [Findings](https://grothendieck.commutator.io/findings/): results that may not stand in the literature, each with what would settle it, and the statements proved in Lean.

## Beside the fonds

- [Quillen](https://grothendieck.commutator.io/quillen/): Daniel Quillen's research notebooks (Clay Mathematics Institute), with the ones that meet the fonds marked.
- [Bourbaki](https://grothendieck.commutator.io/bourbaki/): the Bourbaki archive's catalogue (Archives Henri Poincaré), with the documents that meet the fonds marked.

## The project

- [Method](https://grothendieck.commutator.io/method/): how the notes are transcribed and read, and the limits of the edition.
- [Contribute](https://grothendieck.commutator.io/contribute/): the transcription skills and how to propose a correction.
- [Source code and data](https://github.com/Commutator-IO/grothendieck-project)
